Is it necessary to remove `ReadOnly`?
My mistake. Done.
Can't we use regular `register_property` without a custom getter?

A plain register_property would route the daemon's own poll/readback updates (via set_property) through the same setter callback used for client PATCHes, so we'd need an extra "internal set" flag to tell poll-driven writes apart from real client writes. 
The custom getter keeps the cached member as the single source of truth and avoids that setter re-entry, so I'd prefer to keep it here (same pattern as the PowerCap control).
We use it in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/90189/13/src/nvidia-gpu/NvidiaGpuPowerControl.cpp too.
We haven't added custom set-property handler for the property `PresentSpeedLimitMaxHz` unlike `RequestedSpeedLimitMaxHz`, right?
Yes.
So, can't we use regular register_property without custom get-property handler?
Done for the read-only Present* — switched to plain register_property updated via set_property. The writable Requested* keep the custom getter.

I think we should set `setClockLimitInflight` to false only after the response of the GetClockLimit request (send at the end of this function) is received to avoid lost update problem. We have to distinguish between response handling of period update vs update after set.

Good catch. I added a setClockLimitReadbackPending flag — only the post-set read-back clears the in-flight gate, periodic polls leave it untouched. The error paths (and the case where no read-back can be sent) clear the gate too, so a failed set can't wedge it shut.
Shouldn't this be outside of `if (!requestEncoded)` statement? And wouldn't this be always true since we are setting it to true at line number 383?

Moved the gate-release out of sendGetClockLimitRequest. It's now handled in handleSetClockLimitResponse.
(You're right it wasn't strictly always-true, since update()'s periodic poll also calls this with the flag unset — but the check was confusing to begin with, so it's gone now.)
Shouldn't we set this to false only after the getting the response from the device?
Done
